work: The Æneid of Virgil translated into English prose

Æneas.what: Æneas despairs in Juno's storm, lands in Libya and meets Venus, then Dido.
Æneas narrates Troy's fall, flees with Anchises and loses Creusa.
Æneas shelters in the cave with Dido, then obeys Mercury and sails from Carthage.
Æneas plucks the golden bough and descends to the underworld, meeting Anchises in Elysium.
Æneas seeks Evander's alliance on Tiber's advice and receives Vulcan's shield.
Æneas is wounded and healed, then kills Turnus on seeing Pallas' belt.

Ascanius.what: Ascanius shames the Trojan women who burn the ships and leads the boys' game.
Ascanius wounds Silvia's tame stag, igniting the first fighting.
Ascanius kills Numanus in his first kill, then Apollo restrains him from fighting.

Juno.what: Juno bribes Æolus to raise a storm against the Trojan fleet.
Juno bargains with Venus and arranges the storm that unites Dido and Æneas.
Juno sends Iris to incite the Trojan women to burn the ships.
Juno sends Allecto to stir up war and herself opens the gates of War.
Juno pleads in council and lures Turnus away with a phantom Æneas.
Juno speaks to Juturna and agrees with Jupiter that the Latians keep their name.

Jove.what: Jove foretells Rome's rise to Venus and sends Mercury to soften Dido.
Jove sends Mercury to order Æneas to sail for Italy.
Jove sends rain that quenches the burning ships.
Jupiter calls the council, rebukes the gods and declares himself neutral.
Jupiter decrees with Juno the Latians' future, and a Fury is sent against Turnus.

Anchises.what: Anchises refuses to leave Troy until a flame and falling star convince him.
Anchises interprets oracles, and dies at Drepanum.
Anchises appears in a dream and urges Æneas to visit him below.
Anchises explains the souls' cycle and shows Æneas the future heroes of Rome.

Venus.what: Venus pleads with Jupiter and meets Æneas disguised as a huntress.
Venus stops Æneas from killing Helen and shows him the gods destroying Troy.
Venus begs Neptune for safe passage for the Trojans.
Venus wins arms from Vulcan and presents the shield to Æneas.
Venus pleads for the Trojans in Jupiter's council.
Venus heals Æneas' wound with dittany and restores his weapons.

Achates.what: Achates accompanies Æneas ashore and into Carthage hidden in mist.
Achates is first to cry out the sight of Italy.

Turnus.what: Allecto inflames Turnus to war, and he rejects the Trojans' claim.
Turnus attacks the camp, fires the fleet, breaks in and escapes by the Tiber.
Turnus kills Pallas and takes his belt, then is carried away by Juno's phantom.
Turnus answers Drances and accepts single combat.
Turnus insists on the duel, fights Æneas and is killed.

Messapus.what: Messapus is introduced as invulnerable son of Neptune in the catalogue.
Messapus fights with Turnus in the siege of the Trojan camp.

Dido.what: Dido welcomes the Trojans and asks Æneas to tell his tale.
Dido loves Æneas, is abandoned, curses him and kills herself on the pyre.
Dido refuses Æneas in the underworld and flees to Sychæus.

Mezentius.what: Mezentius fights fiercely, is wounded, sees Lausus die and welcomes death.
Mezentius' arms are dedicated as a trophy to Mars.

Pallas.what: Pallas challenges the Trojans and is sent with Æneas by Evander.
Pallas rallies the Arcadians and is killed by Turnus, who takes his belt.
Pallas' body is carried home in procession and mourned by Evander.
Pallas' belt on Turnus moves Æneas to kill him.

Mnestheus.what: Mnestheus captains the Shark in the ship race.

Apollo.what: Apollo's oracle at Delos sends the Trojans to seek their ancient mother land.
Apollo praises Ascanius, then disguised as Butes tells him to stop fighting.
Apollo hears Arruns' prayer but grants only half of it.

Lavinia.what: Lavinia's burning hair is a portent of the foreign son-in-law.

Neptune.what: Neptune rebukes the winds and calms the sea.
Neptune promises safe passage at the cost of one life.
Neptune speeds the Trojans past Circe's shore.

Iris.what: Iris cuts Dido's lock of hair to free her soul.
Iris, disguised as Beroe, rouses the Trojan women to burn the ships.
Iris tells Turnus that Æneas is away and urges him to attack.

Hector.what: Hector's ghost warns Æneas to flee and entrusts him with the gods.

Hercules.what: Evander tells how Hercules killed the monster Cacus.

Ilioneus.what: Ilioneus pleads the Trojans' cause before Dido.
Ilioneus speaks for the Trojans before Latinus.

Latinus.what: Latinus consults Faunus, welcomes the Trojans, then yields to war.
Latinus convenes the council and proposes peace with the Trojans.
Latinus pleads with Turnus and swears the treaty.

Palinurus.what: Palinurus is drugged by Sleep and thrown overboard.
Palinurus' shade speaks to Æneas at the Styx.

Priam.what: Priam spares Sinon, and is killed by Pyrrhus at the altar.

Sergestus.what: Sergestus wrecks the Centaur on the rocks in the ship race.

Tarchon.what: Tarchon allies with Æneas, but his ship is wrecked at the landing.
Tarchon rebukes the Tuscans and seizes Venulus.

Acestes.what: Acestes welcomes the Trojans, goads Entellus, and his arrow bursts into flame.

Amata.what: Allecto maddens Amata, who raves as a Bacchante.
Amata pleads with Turnus, then hangs herself.

Augustus Cæsar.what: Augustus leads at Actium on Æneas' shield.

Cybele.what: Cybele's voice frees her pine ships, turning them into sea-goddesses.

Bitias.what: Bitias opens the gate to Turnus and is killed.

Camilla.what: Camilla offers to meet the cavalry, fights bravely and is killed by Arruns.

Cloanthus.what: Cloanthus wins the ship race with divine help.

Euryalus.what: Euryalus joins Nisus on a night raid and is killed.

Evander.what: Evander welcomes Æneas, tells of Cacus, and entrusts Pallas to him.
Evander laments Pallas and asks that Turnus be killed.

Faunus.what: Faunus's oracle tells Latinus to await a foreign son-in-law.

Gyas.what: Gyas throws Menœtes overboard in the ship race.

Helen.what: Helen hides in Vesta's temple, and Æneas is stopped from killing her.

Mercury.what: Mercury rebukes Æneas and warns him again in a dream.

Lausus.what: Lausus dies saving his father Mezentius.

Misenus.what: Misenus is found drowned by Triton and given a pyre and tomb.

Vulcan.what: Vulcan forges Æneas' arms and the shield at Venus' request.

Pyrrhus.what: Pyrrhus kills Polites and then Priam at the altar.

Nisus.what: Nisus trips Salius so Euryalus can win the race.
Nisus volunteers for the night raid and dies over Euryalus.

Numanus.what: Numanus boasts and is killed by Ascanius.

Polites.what: Polites is killed by Pyrrhus before his parents.

Tiber.what: Tiber appears to Æneas in a dream and advises alliance with Evander.
Tiber receives Turnus and saves him.

Venulus.what: Reports Diomede's refusal of help to Latinus's council, then is seized by Tarchon.

Acca.what: Carries the dying Camilla's message to Turnus after her death.

Achemenides.what: Begs the Trojans for rescue and tells of Polyphemus, left behind by Ulysses.

Æolus.what: Is bribed by Juno with Deiopea and looses the winds to wreck the Trojan fleet.

Æthon.what: Pallas' war horse weeps in the funeral procession.

Allecto.what: Sent by Juno, drives Amata mad, inflames Turnus, starts the war, and is dismissed.

Almo.what: Is the first slain when fighting erupts over the stag.

Andromache.what: Mourns at Hector's false tomb in Buthrotum and tells of Pyrrhus' death.

Anna.what: Persuades Dido to marry Æneas, later builds the pyre and carries her pleas.

Arruns.what: Stalks Camilla, prays to Apollo, kills her with a spear, and is shot by Opis.

Cacus.what: Fire-breathing monster who steals Hercules' cattle and is killed by him.

Caieta.what: Æneas's nurse Caieta dies and is buried on the coast.

Celæno.what: Prophesies that the Trojans will eat their tables before building their city.

Charon.what: Is persuaded by the golden bough to ferry Aeneas across the Styx.

Coroebus.what: Tries to rescue Cassandra and dies, betrayed by Trojan darts.

Creusa.what: Is lost in the flight from Troy; her ghost foretells Hesperia to Æneas.

Cupid.what: Disguised as Ascanius, inflames Dido with love at the banquet.

Cymodoce.what: Warns Æneas and urges him to arm.

Dares.what: Challenges all to a boxing match and is beaten by Entellus.

Deïphobe.what: The Sibyl, seized by Apollo, prophesies and guides Aeneas through the underworld.

Deiphobus.what: Mutilated Deiphobus tells Aeneas how Helen betrayed him on Troy's last night.

Diana.what: Diana tells Opis Camilla's story and sends her to avenge Camilla.

Diomede.what: Diomede, at Arpi, refuses to fight the Trojans, as Venulus reports.

Drances.what: Drances praises Æneas, then presses the case against Turnus and demands he yield Lavinia.

Entellus.what: Old Entellus, goaded by Acestes, beats Dares at boxing and kills the bull for Eryx.

Fame.what: Fame spreads the rumour of Dido and Æneas and rouses Iarbas.

Galæsus.what: Galæsus is killed while pleading for peace as fighting erupts.

Helenus.what: Helenus welcomes the Trojans at Buthrotum and prophesies their route and dangers.

Iapis.what: Iapis tries to extract the arrow from Æneas but cannot.

Iarbas.what: Iarbas, angered by the rumour, prays to Jove against Dido and Æneas.

Juturna.what: Disguised as Camers, Juturna stirs the Rutulians and the truce is broken.
Left by Turnus, Juturna helps him in the duel and is driven away by a Fury.

Laocoon.what: Laocoon warns against the horse, hurls a spear at it, and dies with his sons.

Liger.what: Liger is killed by Æneas in his rampage.

Lucagus.what: Lucagus is killed by Æneas in his rampage.

Magus.what: Magus begs for mercy and is killed by Æneas.

Menœtes.what: Gyas throws the pilot Menœtes overboard during the ship race.

Nautes.what: Nautes counsels Æneas to leave the weary behind in Acesta.

Opis.what: Sent by Diana, Opis shoots Arruns dead to avenge Camilla.

Pandarus.what: Pandarus and Bitias open the gate, letting Turnus into the Trojan camp.

Panthus.what: Panthus brings news and joins Æneas and the young warriors in Troy's street fighting.

Sleep.what: Sleep, disguised as Phorbas, drugs Palinurus and throws him overboard.

Polydorus.what: Polydorus speaks from the bleeding bushes in Thrace and tells of his murder for gold.

Polyphemus.what: The blinded Polyphemus appears on the shore and the Trojans flee.

Pyrgo.what: Pyrgo, the aged royal nurse, unmasks Iris disguised as Beroe among the Trojan women.

Rhamnes.what: Rhamnes, the Rutulian augur, is killed asleep by Nisus and Euryalus.

Rhœtus.what: Rhœtus is killed by Euryalus in the Rutulian camp.

Salius.what: Salius is tripped by Nisus in the foot-race and is compensated by Æneas.

Serranus.what: Serranus is killed asleep by Nisus and Euryalus.

Silvia.what: Silvia's tame stag is wounded by Ascanius, sparking the first fighting.

Sinon.what: Sinon feigns desertion with a false tale and persuades the Trojans to take in the horse.
Sinon opens the horse and lets the Greeks out at night.

Sulmo.what: Sulmo is killed by Nisus's spear while Nisus tries to save Euryalus.

Tagus.what: Tagus is killed by Nisus's spear while Nisus tries to save Euryalus.

Tolumnius.what: Tolumnius, after an omen, throws a spear and breaks the truce.

Volscens.what: Volscens' horsemen catch Euryalus; Nisus kills Volscens in revenge.
